correctness.rationale: The defect is a persistent transition rule at vertex zero, which is also the starting site. For 2≤k≤n−1, the first of the adjacent vertices k−1,k to be hit determines which of the clockwise and counterclockwise arcs through zero has already been traversed before either absorber is hit. Thus L≥k iff k−1 wins; if k wins, every still-unvisited vertex is at most k−1. Independently derive the splitting law by excursions from zero: each attempt succeeds clockwise with probability p/(k−1), counterclockwise with q/(n−k), and otherwise returns to zero. Conditioning on the first successful attempt gives (1) and covers adjacent-to-zero absorbers (arm length one). The k=1 tail is 1, and the k=n tail is 0. Subtracting consecutive tails gives numerator (n−1)pq and D_(k+1)−D_k=q−p gives the strict mass monotonicities for unequal biases. Differentiation in p gives the positive tail derivative for nontrivial cuts. Rounding the cut at (n−1)u gives the stated CDF limit, continuous also at u=0,1. The step density obtained by multiplying each mass by n−1 converges uniformly because its two denominator factors are ≥min(p,q)>0 and the mesh width vanishes. Except at p=q, its limiting density crosses one once where p+(q−p)u=√(pq), at u=√p/(√p+√q). The absolute difference of the two CDFs there equals the claimed limiting TV. At p=q the discrete law is exactly uniform. Replay: RESULT.md §§1–5 and the excursion probabilities above. evidence: A last-discovery tail is an adjacent absorbing-vertex race on an unwrapped interval. Classical exit probabilities yield the pieces; the direction of the first step is biased on every excursion, not merely at initial time.

The closest conductance formula (93e0815cb503) uses a related reduction of a point mass to two gambler's-ruin events, but assumes positive edge conductances. The product of the present chain's clockwise-to-reverse ratios around the cycle is p/q, unequal to one unless p=q.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The biased chain cannot be rewritten as a reversible positive-conductance cycle by changing edge labels or scale. Similarly, a deterministic time-dependent bias does not implement feedback based on the walker's current vertex.

value.rationale: The conclusion measures a global effect of one local perturbation: it changes the shape of the last-discovery distribution and leaves a nonzero, exactly quantified TV distance without concentrating the endpoint near the start. This separates the one-defect mechanism from fixed homogeneous drift and from uniform last discovery. The harmonic calculation is elementary, but the macroscopic comparison and explicit benchmark for spatially inhomogeneous cycle models are the substantive content.
